question.text: SEBI places concentration limits on Category III AIFs. The fund may invest not more than what percentage of its Investable Funds or NAV in a single investee company (normal Cat III, not Large Value Fund)?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Ch 11.2.4.1 (Activist Strategy), SEBI restricts Cat III AIFs to not more than 10% of Investable Funds or NAV in one single investee company. For Large Value Funds (LVF), this relaxation is up to 20% per investee. **The Trap:** 5% is the tighter Cat I/II limit for certain activities. 20% is the LVF relaxation, not the normal limit. 25% is not a SEBI concentration number for Cat III. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-B tests 10% concentration at product level. XIX-C tests the LVF relaxation distinction (10% vs 20%). **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For Activist strategies, the 10% cap is often binding. Structure such funds as LVF at launch to unlock the 20% cap — but note LVF has INR 70 cr minimum commitment per investor.
